transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I suppose I'm here because things got a bit out of hand recently. I took on this project for the historical society, and... well, I acted like I could run the entire fundraiser all by myself. I was starting up all these new quilt designs, calling volunteers left and right, drawing up schedules, and just promising deadlines that I couldn't possibly meet. It all just sort of caught up with me.
Have you found yourself acting like this in other situations before?

Honestly, no, not that I can think of. I mean, I've always liked being involved in my community groups, but... I don't think I've ever gone quite this overboard before. Usually I know my limits and just stick to my normal routine. So this whole thing was pretty unusual for me.
Did you feel like you were able to stop yourself from taking on more and more responsibilities with the fundraiser, or did it feel like it was hard to control?

It felt really hard to control. I just couldn't seem to stop myself. Every time someone brought up a new idea or a problem, I just jumped right in and said I'd handle it. It was like I was on autopilot, just saying yes to everything, even when a part of me knew I was already in over my head. I didn't even think about slowing down until it all crashed down on me.
Have you ever had issues with impulsivity in other areas of your life, such as spending money or impulsive decisions?

No, not really. I'm usually pretty careful with my money, and I don't really make big decisions on the fly. Like I said, I usually just stick to my normal routine. That's why this whole thing with the fundraiser was so strange for me.
Did you experience any feelings of euphoria or excitement when you were taking on all these responsibilities?

Yes, I did. At first, I felt... well, almost glowing. It was like every idea I had was just wonderful. But, um, if anyone questioned me or my plans, I got really snappish. I just acted like they were standing in the way.
Did you feel like you were somehow special or uniquely qualified to handle all these responsibilities with the fundraiser?

Yes, I did. I, um... I truly believed my heritage quilt ideas were going to put our little town on the map. It just felt like I had finally found the thing that only I could make happen. I really thought I was the only person who could see the whole vision and do it right.
Have you experienced any periods of feeling sad, empty, or depressed over the past few weeks?

No, I haven't. I really haven't felt down or sad at all lately. If anything, it's just been... well, all that energy and focus I had with the fundraiser. So, no, I haven't had any periods of feeling empty or depressed.
Was this feeling of being almost glowing and having wonderful ideas constant while you were working on the fundraiser?

Well, I'm not really sure if it was constant every single minute, but... yeah, it pretty much lasted the whole time. I didn't really have any breaks from feeling that way until the fundraiser was over.
Did you ever have a day where you didn't feel that glowing or excited about the fundraiser?

No, not really. I mean... I can't think of a single day where I woke up and didn't feel that excitement. Like I was saying, it just stayed with me the whole time. There wasn't really a day where it stopped or faded until the whole thing was finally over.
Did your excited and glowing feeling ever vary in intensity from one moment to another while you were working on the fundraiser?

I'm not really sure. I mean... I didn't really notice if it went up or down from minute to minute. It just felt like a steady level of energy to me. I was so busy getting things done that I wasn't really paying attention to the exact intensity of it, you know? It just felt strong the whole time.
Did your excited and glowing feeling with the fundraiser ever go away for a little while and then come back?
No, it didn't really go away and come back. It was just... there. The whole time I was working on it, that feeling stayed with me. It didn't take any breaks.
Did you feel this impulsivity in other areas of your life during the same time period as the fundraiser?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I was just so focused on the fundraiser that I wasn't really doing much else. Everything was going into that one project, so I didn't really have the time or the chance to be impulsive with anything else, you know? It was all just about getting the event put together.
Did you act impulsively in any other areas of your life during the time you were working on the fundraiser?

No, like I was just saying, I really didn't. I was just so completely wrapped up in the fundraiser. I didn't have the time or energy to do anything else, impulsive or not. Everything I had was going straight into that project.
Was your impulsivity during that time limited to just the fundraiser, or did it affect other parts of your life as well?

I feel like I'm repeating myself a bit here, but yes, it was strictly limited to the fundraiser. Like I said, I didn't really have anything else going on right then. My whole focus was just on that one event, so it didn't affect any other parts of my life.
Did you have any periods of significantly decreased need for sleep during the time you were working on the fundraiser?
No, I don't think so. I was sleeping about the same as usual, maybe a little less just because I was busy, but I wasn't staying up all night or anything like that. I still needed my rest.
Did you feel like your thoughts were racing during the time you were working on the fundraiser?

Yes, they definitely were. My mind would just... race. I'd be thinking about quilt blocks one second, and then before I could even finish that thought, I'd be on to the donor lists, and then the church announcements. It was all moving so quickly that I couldn't hold onto one thought long enough to actually finish it.
Did you have any similar episodes of increased energy and impulsivity before the fundraiser?
No, I really haven't. That was... well, it was the only time anything like that has ever happened to me. I've always just been pretty steady, you know? Nothing like that before.
Do you think you could have another episode like the one you had with the fundraiser in the future?
I... I really don't know. I hope not. It's not something I've really thought about happening again, since it had never happened before. But I guess I'm not entirely sure.
